memory_update.text: HMDPF/HPS.A should remain a priority candidate for the dry-type-transformer and power-quality node because company disclosures directly match dry-type transformers, power-quality products, related magnetics, digital infrastructure, and backlog growth.

POWL is not a dry-type transformer pure-play but is a strong adjacent candidate for switchgear, e-houses, power-control rooms, bus duct, and engineered power-distribution bottlenecks; verify data-center and utility order mix.

AMSC adds a less obvious power-quality lane through STATCOMs, voltage control, harmonic filters, and reactive compensation; survival in later layers depends on confirming grid-product revenue/backlog share.
HUBB should be treated as a reference/competitive anchor for scaled electrical and utility infrastructure exposure, not as the primary underfollowed discovery candidate.

PPSI appeared in searches but should be handled as a speculative shadow candidate only: current evidence points more to mobile/critical power and distributed generation after sale of electrical infrastructure assets, not direct dry-type transformer exposure.

node: Dry-type transformers, power-quality products, and specialty magnetics
summary: Expanded the universe around dry-type transformers, power-quality systems, specialty magnetics, switchgear, and adjacent grid-power conditioning. The underfollowed lane is strongest in Hammond Power Solutions, Powell Industries, and American Superconductor: all have more direct exposure to bottlenecked electrical-infrastructure products than broad mega-cap electrification leaders. Hubbell is included as a reference/competitive anchor because it has public-market scale and utility/electrical-product breadth, but it is less pure than the small/mid-cap discovery lane. No buy/sell view is implied.
